answer: A magnetic coupling protocol curbs Sybil attacks in marine agent swarms. Candidate nodes must physically clamp onto a submerged ferrous piling beneath a harbor jetty to measure localized inductive resonance. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of manufacturing and deploying dedicated robotic hulls with magnetic actuators for each identity. However, shifting salinity across the daily tide perturbs eddy-current baselines, occasionally causing false rejections of valid agents.
